summary: Well-designed, artifact-backed preregistered confirmatory run that produced an evidence-grounded ceiling/null outcome. Solid execution traceability (extensive hashes, per-episode scoring JSONs, provider traces, manifests). However the preregistered primary estimand (AUC comparison of a trained composite vs best submetric) cannot be recomputed from the supplied evidence because the test labels are constant (no positive outage examples) and two preregistered artifacts (serialized trained-composite-model weights and consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV) were not persisted. The manuscript documents these facts, but it currently still frames the result as a “confirmatory” test of the preregistered discriminative hypothesis; that framing, plus the missing persisted artifacts, are the main issues preventing finalisation.
critical_issues: The preregistered primary estimand (AUC-ROC comparison of the trained composite vs best single submetric) is uncomputable from the supplied evidence: the held-out test contains zero positive outage labels (n11=200,n10=0,n01=0,n00=0), so ROC/AUPRC comparisons cannot be formed.

Two preregistered artifacts required to reproduce the primary discriminative analysis are missing from the evidence bundle: (a) the serialized trained-composite-model weights; (b) the consolidated per-episode submetric summary CSV — their absence prevents deterministic recomputation of the preregistered AUC-based comparison from the supplied bundle.

Manuscript framing/title uses language ("Confirmatory") that may misleadingly imply the preregistered AUC-based hypothesis was tested and adjudicated; given the uncomputable primary estimand this must be corrected to avoid overclaiming.
required_revisions: Explicitly state (prominently in the Abstract and Introduction) that the preregistered AUC-ROC primary estimand was not tested because the held-out test set contained no positive outage examples; remove or reword any phrasing that implies the AUC-based hypothesis was confirmed or reject/accepted.

Add a concise, artifact-grounded explanation for why the two required artifacts (serialized trained-composite-model weights and consolidated per-episode submetric CSV) were not persisted (root cause), and confirm that no other preregistered artifacts are missing. If the omission was accidental, state that fact and provide the rationale and UI/storage logs or manifest pointer if available in the evidence bundle.

Provide a deterministic, stepwise reproduction recipe (file paths, exact command(s)/script names, model-training hyperparameters and random seeds, preprocessing steps, and output file paths) that allows an independent reader to reconstruct the composite-score training and test application from the existing per-episode scoring JSONs and manifests (execution/scoring/*.json, execution/provider_calls/*, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json). If a ready reconstruction script exists in the evidence bundle, cite its exact path and hash; if not, provide the exact pseudocode/commands that would be used so readers can reproduce deterministically from the retained raw artifacts.

Revise title and abstract to avoid the wordings that could be read as having executed the preregistered AUC comparison; emphasize that the principal contribution is methodological (artifact-backed null ceiling effect and reproducibility lessons) rather than a discriminative-model validation.

Update the Results and Conclusion paragraphs to (a) report clearly which preregistered estimands were actually evaluated (paired success-rate difference) versus which were uncomputable (AUC-ROC), and (b) discuss the implications for the original hypotheses and for future study design.
optional_revisions: If possible without adding new external data, add a short appendix (≤1 paragraph) enumerating the exact hyperparameter grid and CV procedure used during the (planned) L2 logistic-regression training (penalty values, CV fold assignment method), and reference where those values are recorded in the preregistration JSON so readers can deterministically retrain from raw submetrics.

Discuss concrete, minimal ways to seed nontrivial positive outage rates in future synthetic task banks (examples: seeded adversarial perturbations, stochastic emulator fault-injection schedules, or a small set of adversarial tasks), and quantify how such augmentations would restore computability for the preregistered AUC estimand.

Add a brief table mapping the most relevant persisted artifact paths and hashes (execution/scoring/, execution/provider_calls/, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json) to the specific pieces of information needed to recreate the composite (e.g., which fields in execution/scoring/*.json correspond to verifier coverage, canary-sim pass, rollback success estimate, LLM confidence, abstention utility).
